Latin word

intrōdūcō

intrōdūcō, intrōdūcere, intrōdūxī, intrōductum

verb, third conjugation, transitive; with in and the accusative · Conjugation on Wiktionary

bring in, introduce (a custom, an idea)

In this lexicon

  • introduce

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Tusc. 5.10: in domūs etiam intrōdūxit; Cic. Fam. 16.21.3: hāc intrōductā cōnsuētūdine; Traupman 334

Examples

  • Sōcratēs autem prīmus philosophiam dēvocāvit ē caelō et in urbibus conlocāvit et in domūs etiam intrōdūxit

    Socrates was the first to call philosophy down from the sky; he settled it in cities and even brought it into people’s homes.Cic. Tusc. 5.10

    In the entry for introduce

  • hāc intrōductā cōnsuētūdine saepe īnscientibus nōbīs et cēnantibus obrēpit

    Now that this has become our custom, he often steals in on us unannounced while we are at dinner.Cic. Fam. 16.21.3

    In the entry for introduce

  • tunc hymnī et psalmī ut canerentur secundum mōrem orientālium partium, nē populus maerōris taediō contābēsceret, īnstitūtum est

    It was then that the singing of hymns and psalms after the custom of the East was introduced, so that the people should not waste away in weariness and grief.Aug. Conf. 9.7.15
